Exercise 1

Part 1

You will need a CS undergraduate linux account for this class. Here are options for obtaining an account. We will be using them in class starting this Friday!

  • If you have one already, then use that.
  • If you are a declared CS major/minor, get a “permanent account” from the CS IT website according to the instructions posted there (download form, fill in your info, email to support@cs.jhu.edu). You will then need to meet with an IT staff member to “pick up” your account information.
  • Otherwise, send “all instructors” a private post on Piazza with subject “Request for a temp cs account”. Include your name, JHED ID, and course section number in the request post. We will get back to you with the user name and password for a temporary account to use this semester once your course registration is verified.

Next, everyone should log into Canvas, go to this course, then click through to Piazza in the left menu. Carefully read through the account and lab usage policies posted in Piazza @6 and the course posting policies in Piazza @9.

Part 2

Create a Github account and provide us with the user name:

  1. Create a free account at Github, if you do not have one already.

  2. Once created, fill in this Getting Started Form as soon as possible.

  3. Look out for an invitation email from Github in the mailbox of the email address you used to sign up for Github. Accept the invitation to join the course Github organization.

Caution

Do not submit the above form more than once!

Caution

If you do not accept the invitation, you will not be able to access the starter codes and we will not be able to provision you a private repository that you will need for the remainder of the course. Once you accept the invitation, you will be given a private repo under jhu-ip organization which you will use as your personal space for the exercises and homeworks throughout the semester.

Part 3

Read through the first two items in the Resources section for today: cliff notes for using Unix, and a longer Unix/Linux Tutorial. We will be working in this environment all semester.
